answer: An agent economy can make every identity a vertex in a live graph of mutual work: each edge between two agents needs a fresh, jointly produced proof of real collaboration, sealed behind a walnut-hard check that only opens when both sides contribute something the other can verify. A fake starts isolated, and forging an edge costs a distinct piece of verifiable joint work with a real counterparty, so each extra fake costs more than the last. A ferrous anchor pins every edge to a tamper-evident public log, so a Sybil ring cannot clone one proof across many identities or buy standing in bulk.
